title: Proton Irradiation of Vascular Structures and Circulating Biomarkers of Endothelial Damage in Routine Clinical Practice: A Prospective Exploratory Study
content: Background/Objectives: Blood vessels are not delineated as organs at risk and the residual exposure of the vasculature under proton therapy is rarely measured. We quantified it and tested whether it is accompanied by changes in circulating markers of endothelial damage, matrix remodelling and NETosis. Methods: Twenty-four patients receiving a proton component underwent 4D-flow magnetic resonance imaging of the vascular tree. Vessels were segmented on the planning dataset and the effective dose to circulating immune cells (EDIC) and the integral dose to vessels (IDV) computed from their dose–volume histograms. P-selectin, MMP-1, -2, -7, -9 and -10, TIMP-1, citrullinated histone H3 (H3Cit) and endothelial microvesicles were measured before and after treatment and compared with paired t-tests. Results: Median EDIC was 1.29 Gy (range 0.1–4.2) and median IDV 0.49 Gy·L (0.01–2.9). MMP-9 rose from 29.9 ± 16.5 to 50.1 ± 39.0 ng/mL (+20.2; 95% CI 2.3 to 38.0; p = 0.028) and citrullinated histone H3 from 10.7 ± 9.6 to 14.4 ± 11.3 ng/mL (+3.7; 95% CI 0.4 to 6.9; p = 0.028); endothelial microvesicles rose by 63% (p = 0.087). P-selectin and MMP-1, -2, -7 and -10 did not change. TIMP-1 fell by 12.4% (p = 0.183), so the rise in protease went unmatched by its inhibitor; the per-patient MMP-9/TIMP-1 ratio did not change significantly (p = 0.781). Neither dose metric separated responders from non-responders. Conclusions: Proton irradiation of vascular structures at routine doses is accompanied by a measurable rise in markers of NETosis and matrix remodelling, MMP-9 rising while its inhibitor TIMP-1 fell. No dose–response relationship was demonstrable at this sample size. Delineating vessels as organs at risk is the prerequisite for testing one.
